skill.description: Turn user-provided personal finance records into a local interactive report with spending, income, transfers and cash movement in English or Chinese. Use for statement-based finance charts and period comparisons, not bank-account actions or investment advice.
skill.summary: Visualize authorized financial records in English or Chinese with local charts, period comparisons, and transaction details.

content.user_title: Visualize Personal Finances in a Local Report
content.value_statement: Financial records can make spending, income, and transfers difficult to compare. This skill prepares reconciled data and displays local interactive reports with period controls and transaction details.
actual_capabilities: Render normalized JSON or CSV as interactive local reports with overview, spending, income, and transfer views.
Compare daily, weekly, monthly, and yearly periods within confirmed source coverage.
Apply confirmed personal shares, exact full-refund mappings, and bounded transfer settlements while retaining original bank amounts.
Inspect transaction details with text search, category and account filters, and sortable table columns.
Display English or Simplified Chinese interfaces with ring charts, area charts, and an alternative bar-chart view.
Serve reports from memory through tokenized loopback URLs or create explicitly requested standalone local HTML exports.
limitations: Raw bank exports require explicit field mapping; PDF extraction depends on authorized tools outside this skill.
Each report supports one currency with two decimal places; currency conversion and automatic partial-refund spending adjustments are unavailable.
Python 3.10 or later and a modern browser are required; input is limited to 25 MiB and 100,000 transactions.
The skill does not connect bank accounts, execute payments, modify subscriptions, or provide investment advice.

use_cases.title: Review Household Spending
use_cases.description: Compare monthly spending categories, recurring services, and daily costs using authorized household records.

use_cases.title: Separate Freelance Income and Transfers
use_cases.description: Inspect confirmed income separately from unknown receipts, repayments, and internal account movements.

use_cases.title: Review Shared Expenses
use_cases.description: Apply confirmed personal shares and refund mappings while keeping original bank amounts available for verification.

prompt_templates.title: Explore a Fictional Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an English report using only the bundled fictional demo data. Open the temporary local report without exporting files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: explore charts without supplying personal records.

prompt_templates.title: Review Supplied Records
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my supplied normalized CSV for the confirmed period [start] through [end] in [currency]. Ask about unresolved classifications before producing final charts.
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic: inspect an existing normalized dataset.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Shared Spending
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare monthly spending from my authorized records in Simplified Chinese. Confirm personal shares and internal movements; preserve original amounts and disclose coverage gaps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: compare periods with shared costs.

prompt_templates.title: Reconcile Refunds and Repayments
prompt_templates.prompt: Reconcile my supplied JSON records and ask about ambiguous refunds or repayments. Apply only confirmed mappings, verify totals, and deliver a memory-only report.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: reconcile related transactions before reporting.

output_examples.input: Fictional example: a USD 1,000 rent payment has a confirmed 50% personal share, plus USD 80 of personal groceries.
output: Bank-date outflow: USD 1,080, assuming no other transactions or adjustments.
Transaction details retain the original rent amount and the confirmed personal share.

output_examples.input: Fictional example: a USD 84 February purchase has a confirmed full USD 84 refund in March, with both transactions supplied.
output: The confirmed purchase contributes zero to February personal spending.
Bank-date cash movement retains the USD 84 February outflow and USD 84 March inflow.
Transaction details identify the full-refund match and retain the original amounts.

best_practices: Confirm source coverage, currency, date interpretation, and amount signs before preparing a report.
Resolve uncertain classifications, shares, refunds, and settlements with the user before finalizing affected charts.
Use account aliases and memory-only delivery; review host retention settings and keep explicitly requested exports private.
anti_patterns: Do not classify every receipt as income or infer refunds, repayments, or duplicates from matching dates and amounts alone.
Do not put private records in the skill repository, public issues, shell arguments, or saved demonstration screenshots.
Do not combine currencies, invent missing coverage, or present a subset of accounts as a complete financial picture.

faq.question: Which input formats are supported?
faq.answer: The renderer accepts normalized JSON and CSV. Raw bank exports need explicit mapping, and PDF extraction requires an available authorized tool.

faq.question: Does the skill require bank credentials?
faq.answer: No. It works with authorized records supplied for the task and does not connect bank accounts or execute financial actions.

faq.question: Is processing completely offline?
faq.answer: The renderer uses no remote assets or telemetry. Agent hosts may retain supplied data; a separately requested update check contacts GitHub.

faq.question: What happens to reports after use?
faq.answer: Default reports remain in process memory until the server stops. Browser artifacts, host transcripts, and explicitly exported HTML may persist.

faq.question: How are refunds and shared expenses handled?
faq.answer: Confirmed shares affect personal spending. Confirmed full refunds cancel matched purchase spending; partial or unmatched refunds remain separate.

faq.question: Can reports combine currencies or switch languages?
faq.answer: Create separate reports for different currencies; only currencies with two decimal places are supported. The interface supports English and Simplified Chinese.
